Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

prevent verb

also stop (someone doing something), keep from, hinder, stand in the way, deter, prevention, be in the way, get in the way

classical

Cic. Div. Caec. 33: quod potuistī prohibēre, nē fieret (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Off. 1.52: nōn prohibēre aquā prōfluente

prohibeō, prohibēre, prohibuī, prohibitum

verb, second conjugation: the person kept off in the accusative, what he is kept from in the ablative (with or without ā); or nē, quōminus and the subjunctive · Conjugation on Wiktionary

keep off, prevent

Literally “hold in front”, and so hold off, keep away: the plain word for stopping a thing from happening or a person from doing it. It also means “forbid” (nēmō hīc prohibet nec vetat, Plaut. Curc. 1.1.33, Lewis & Short), so the context decides between “prevent” and “prohibit”; for forbidding see vetō.

Other words

  • impediō, impedīre, impedīvī, impedītum — hinder, get in the way

    verb, fourth conjugation: with an accusative, or nē, quōminus (quīn after a negative) and the subjunctive · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 60: nec aetās impedit, quōminus agrī colendī studia teneāmus (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fat. 1: casus quīdam, nē facerem, impedīvit (Lewis & Short); Traupman 328; Traupman 404 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Literally “shackle the feet”: of whatever gets in the way, business, age, the weather, a chance event. Its literal sense, “entangle”, and the poets’ “encircle, wreathe” (Hor. C. 1.4.9) are less common (Lewis & Short).

  • dēterreō, dēterrēre, dēterruī, dēterritum — deter, put off

    verb, second conjugation: the person in the accusative, with ā and the ablative, or nē, quōminus and the subjunctive · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.117: hominēs adulēscentēs ā dīcendī studiō (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Prevent by frightening or talking someone out of it: “discourage”, not “make impossible”.

Examples

  • quod potuistī prohibēre, nē fieret

    what you could have prevented from happeningCic. Div. Caec. 33 (Lewis & Short)

  • nōn prohibēre aquā prōfluente, patī ab igne ignem capere, sī quī velit

    not to keep anyone from running water, to let him take fire from your fire if he wantsCic. Off. 1.52

  • nec aetās impedit, quōminus agrī colendī studia teneāmus

    nor does age prevent us from keeping up our interest in farmingCic. Sen. 60 (Lewis & Short)

  • Quid tē impedit quōminus veniās?

    What’s stopping you from coming?composed

  • obvius esse

    to be in the wayTraupman 404

  • obstāre (+ dative)

    to be in the way, hinderTraupman 404

See also ban, don’t!, allow, avoid, stop.
